clue.text: Granny with degree overcoming president with spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overcoming another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
George Bush, US president
KA is the ancient Egyptian spirit or soul, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: An elderly woman with a degree gets the better of a president, aided by a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian word for grandmother, also used for an old woman in a headscarf.

clue.text: I solve Paul ultimately to become hero

parts.note: to do a puzzle is to solve it

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of the setter's name

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that solving his own puzzles will make him a celebrated figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idolised is a person held up as a hero, a worshipped figure.

clue.text: 4's island

definitions.meaning: a knitted top worn over a shirt is a piece of top gear, clothing for the upper body
the largest of the Channel Islands

explanation.walkthrough: 4 is TOP GEAR, read as clothes worn on top. Jersey is also a Channel Island off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen sweater counts as upper-body clothing, and the name is also that of a Channel Island.

clue.text: 5th show?

definitions.meaning: on many cars the fifth is the highest ratio in the gearbox
the BBC motoring programme presented by the entry at 5

explanation.walkthrough: TOP GEAR is the BBC motoring show presented by James May (5), and fifth is the top gear in a typical five-speed car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifth is the highest ratio in a typical gearbox, and the phrase also names a BBC motoring programme.

clue.text: 4's blockage easy to deal with crossing motorway

parts.note: a traffic jam is a blockage

indicators.note: the rearranged letters straddle the motorway, holding it inside
letters to be dealt with are worked over and rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A traffic jam on the motorway, apparently easy enough for the presenter to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to deal with' makes ESAY, and 'crossing' wraps it round the motorway to give ESMAY; the blockage is a traffic one.
explanation.definitionFit: The presenter of the BBC motoring programme at 4, alongside Clarkson and Hammond.

clue.text: With rotten apple full of weevils at first, it's wet and foaming

indicators.note: something rotten has gone bad, so the word before is spoiled into a new order
the apple is full of the letter, so it is placed inside

parts.note: an eater is an eating apple, as opposed to a cooker

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bad apple riddled with weevils is described as soggy and frothy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' gives WHIT, and 'full of' makes EWATER. An eater is an eating apple, as opposed to a cooking apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids where the river churns into froth are described as white water.

clue.text: Motorist's club

definitions.meaning: a motorist is someone at the wheel of a car
the golf club used for long tee shots

explanation.definitionFit: A motorist steers a car, and the long-hitting golf club used off the tee shares the name.

clue.text: US city's coastal feature that is to be removed

parts.note: sand lines a beach
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
to go is to leave or be taken away

explanation.surface: A city's beach is due to be cleared away.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Californian port city near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Hate to stop short, grabbing husband

indicators.note: the shortened word grabs the letter and holds it inside
short means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to abort a process is to stop it

explanation.surface: Someone loathes having to break off suddenly while seizing a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts ABORT to ABOR, and 'grabbing' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or detest something is to feel hatred for it.

clue.text: 4, so speeding 7 might be asked to?

definitions.meaning: a knitted garment worn on the upper body, a piece of top gear

definitions.text: so speeding 7 might be asked to?
definitions.meaning: police signal a speeding motorist to stop at the roadside

explanation.walkthrough: 4 is TOP GEAR read as clothes worn on top; 7 is DRIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is upper-body clothing, and police tell a speeding motorist to stop at the side of the road.

clue.text: Naughty boy flipping taking the biscuit, knocking off princess

indicators.note: flipping turns the name over so it reads backwards

parts.note: Gus is a boy's name

indicators.note: knocking off removes the letters from the front of the word

parts.note: the digestive is a plain wheatmeal biscuit popular in Britain
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A cheeky lad, flipping heck, pinches a biscuit and offends royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns GUS into SUG; 'knocking off' removes DI from DIGESTIVE (a plain British biscuit) to leave GESTIVE. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinting at something risqué; naughty in the saucy, innuendo-laden sense.

clue.text: Cold mountains so?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a landscape thus full of mountains is hilly

explanation.surface: Asking whether high peaks are naturally frosty.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountains tend to be cold places, so the whole clue describes a nippy upland climate.

clue.text: Suggestion of salt in this without appeal?

parts.note: the clue word salt is what you get by sorting again the letters of a word meaning final

explanation.surface: A hint of seasoning in a dish that is entirely unappetising.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: LAST, re-sorted, gives SALT. 'in this' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A final option when nothing else is left, with no further appeal possible.

clue.text: Larva takes my line, backing into weapon

indicators.note: into puts these letters inside the weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
taken as written

indicators.note: backing turns the word round so it reads in reverse

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: A caterpillar seizes my rope, retreating towards a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives WOR, and 'into' puts MYWOR inside the weapon. 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moth caterpillar that travels in vast hordes, devouring crops.

clue.text: Animal by River Thames, swimming

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Some creature paddling along beside London's river.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent often kept as a pet, a specific kind of animal.

clue.text: Very happy to bring up the Church, still

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up raises the letters so they read bottom to top

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
static means still, not moving

explanation.surface: Delighted to raise the subject of the church, nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring up' turns CE into EC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, in a state of rapture.

clue.text: Why suits should be returned after Paul's puzzle

indicators.note: after places the returned letters behind the setter's word

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so his own is 'my'

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the word why
fits means suits

explanation.surface: A setter wonders why his outfits must be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be returned' turns YFITS into STIFY, which goes 'after' MY.
explanation.definitionFit: To mystify is to baffle or perplex, as a puzzle does.

clue.text: Universal fighter in imaginative work, Asia's missing pest controller

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the shortened work
missing means these letters are taken away

parts.note: a fantasia is a freely imaginative musical work, also Disney's film
the continent's name, the possessive adding no letter
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: A general-release war film about a fighter pilot, made without its Asian scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' leaves FANT, and 'in' puts UMIG inside it. Fantasia is also the 1940 Disney film.
explanation.definitionFit: A fumigant is a chemical smoke or vapour used to kill pests.

clue.text: Early stages in thought

parts.note: a fancy is a notion or thought

explanation.surface: Beginnings that exist only in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the earliest period of something, its early stages.

clue.text: See 22
Shed sees crawler in Blair

indicators.note: in puts the insect inside the name

parts.note: Leo Blair, son of former prime minister Tony Blair
an ant is a crawling insect

explanation.surface: A crawler is spotted at the Blair household.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo Blair is the youngest son of Tony Blair, the former British prime minister. 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall.

clue.text: 4's ill-fitting jeans, mockery left and right

indicators.note: ill-fitting clothes are out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The presenter's baggy denims draw ridicule from all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The presenter of TOP GEAR (4) was famous for unflattering jeans.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known presenter of the BBC motoring show at 4.

clue.text: 4's flea?

definitions.meaning: a knitted pullover, a piece of top gear worn on the upper body
a flea is an insect that jumps

explanation.definitionFit: A woolly sweater is upper-body clothing, and a flea is something that leaps.

clue.text: Everyone's drinking water protected by rural establishment — so don't panic!

indicators.note: protected by puts everything inside the farm's letters

parts.note: a farm is a rural establishment

indicators.note: drinking takes the water inside

parts.note: everyone means all, the possessive adding no letter
the sea is water

explanation.surface: Everyone's water supply is safe on the farm, so there is no need to worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' gives ALSEAL, and 'protected by' splits the farm around it. The dash leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning that turns out to be unfounded, so no need for panic.

clue.text: Good to block leaderless Conservative party with many members exposed?

indicators.note: to block means to get in the way of, sitting inside the word
leaderless removes the first letter

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A decent sort tries to obstruct a Conservative gathering that has lost its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' cuts TORY to ORY; 'to block' puts G inside it. 'members' plays on body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild sexual gathering, the 'members' on show being body parts.

clue.text: See 10
Iodine applied to sailors' bones

indicators.note: applied to attaches the letter to the end of the sailors

parts.note: tars are sailors
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Iodine is dabbed on sailors' injured bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small bones of the ankle and foot.

clue.text: Brave revolutionary yearning to take Newcastle etc

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary
a yen is a yearning
NE is the North East of England, where Newcastle lies

explanation.surface: A bold revolutionary longs to capture Newcastle and its region.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Cheyenne are a Native American people.
